summary.text: Keith Jones is the Republican candidate for the Iowa House of Representatives, District 20, in the November 3, 2026 general election, in a race with no incumbent against Democrat Eric Armstrong.
A retired police lieutenant and current Pottawattamie County supervisor, he says he is running on public safety, education and strengthening Iowa families.

paragraphs.text: Keith Jones graduated from Abraham Lincoln High School and earned an associate degree from Iowa Western Community College in 1988.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he worked for the City of Council Bluffs for 29 years, retired as a police lieutenant, served four years as president of the Council Bluffs Fraternal Order of Police lodge, and holds an accounting degree from the University of Nebraska.

He said he is a current Pottawattamie County supervisor who oversees more than 460 full-time employees and a budget of more than $110 million, and that he serves on boards including the Council Bluffs Airport Authority, the Southwest Iowa Juvenile Detention Board, MAPA, the Board of Health and PACE.
Jones advanced from the Republican primary on June 2, 2026.
In the survey, he listed public safety priorities including more Iowa State Patrol hiring, more judges, minimum mandatory sentences and a new state prison.
He also called for raising teacher pay to a minimum of $60,000, more focus on early reading and math, stronger student discipline, and expanded trade education in high schools.
